sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
The window is not a smooth line: operating income fell 58.9% in FY2019 to $5.5 billion, then rose 186.2% in FY2020 to $15.7 billion [F13][F14][D97][D148].

The FY2019 collapse came from an $8.3 billion asset impairment charge, including $6.8 billion of Shave Care goodwill, driven by currency devaluations, slowing category growth and tougher US competition [X109][X112][P62].
FY2020's rebound reflected $8.3 billion of that base-period charge not repeating, plus a 5% sales increase on 4% volume growth [P71][P73].
The US was the steadier engine, growing 4.7% in FY2024 and 2.7% in FY2025, while Non-US fell 1.8% in FY2025 [D529][D532][D507].
In FY2026 Non-US rebounded 6.1% and contributed 3.1pp of the 3.3% total growth, with net sales up 3% on 2% favorable foreign exchange and 1% pricing [D510][D511][D457][P26].
Fabric & Home Care is the largest segment at 34.8% of revenue and added 0.8pp in FY2026, while Beauty added 1.3pp on 7.1% growth [D541][D543][D603][D602].
Operating costs grew 2.1pp faster than revenue in FY2026, at 5.3% cost of revenue growth and 5.5% SG&A growth [D482][D472][D474].
Diluted EPS grew 1.7% against 0.5% net income growth in FY2026 as the diluted share count fell 1.3% [D461][D459][D476].
The FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% sits above the 22.1% window median but below the 24.3% FY2025 high [F30][D648][D647].

The 1.6pp operating-margin decline came from a 1.0pp cost-of-revenue drag and a 0.6pp SG&A drag, as gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix and SG&A rose on marketing spending [D470][D483][D485][P5].
In FY2026 net margin of 18.4% sat 4.3pp below the 22.7% operating margin, with other income of $1.1 billion and a 20.8% tax rate partly offsetting the gap [F50][F30][D693][X108][D443].
The larger FY2019 move was the 11.9pp margin drop to 8.1%, driven by the 12.1pp residual impairment effect rather than operating costs [D109][F23][D125][P62].
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income in FY2026, against a 1.25x window median, and free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x net income [F80][F40][D444][D683][F100][D445].
Free cash flow margin of 17.4% is above the 17.2% window median and well above the 9.2% staples peer median [D441][D654][D673].
Capex rose 16.9% to $4.4 billion, 5.1% of revenue and 1.40x D&A, as investing cash use grew to $4.6 billion on capital expenditures and hedge settlements [F90][D464][D440][D446][F110][P2].
Operating cash flow rose 10% as net earnings plus non-cash items generated about $19.5 billion, with inventory consuming $641 million on higher safety stock and new products [P3].
The company carries net debt of $24.2 billion, net cash of -27.8% of revenue against a -32.3% staples peer median, ranking in the 67th percentile of three peers [D450][D451][D695][D694].
The current ratio of 0.68x is below the 0.72x window median and near the 0.63x FY2023 low, with working capital of -$12.5 billion [F180][D663][D661][F170].
Buybacks of $5.0 billion plus dividends of $10.2 billion were 100.7% of free cash flow in FY2026, and long-term debt fell 8.6% to $22.8 billion [X134][X144][D453][F190][D468].
Return on average equity of 30.1% is below the 44.4% staples peer median, in the 33rd percentile of six peers [D456][D681][D680].
The current ratio has been below 1.0x in every year of the window, at 0.68x in FY2026 [F180][R1].
This is structural for a negative-working-capital consumer staples model rather than a liquidity warning, given $9.9 billion of cash and steady free cash flow [F140][F100].
Buybacks plus dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 at 116.6% and FY2026 at 100.7% [D402][D453][R2].
Payout above free cash flow is covered by the balance sheet but leaves little room if capex keeps rising at 16.9% [D464].
Whether the FY2027 operating margin holds above the 22.1% window median or slips toward the 8.1% FY2019 low, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D648][D646].
Whether capex as a share of revenue stays above the FY2026 5.1% or falls back toward the 3.7% FY2021 level, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D440][D182].
Whether buybacks plus dividends as a share of free cash flow falls below the FY2026 100.7% or rises further above it, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D453].
